about.title: Palm Springs Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Palm Springs draws heavy foot traffic year-round between resort guests, snowbirds, and residents moving through hotel lobbies, pool areas, restaurants, and shopping centers along corridors like Rt 111 and Indian Canyon Drive N. Wet tile near a pool, uneven pavers outside a boutique, poor lighting in a parking structure, or a spill left unaddressed in a grocery aisle can all lead to a serious fall injury. California law generally requires an injured person to show the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazardous condition and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That's why documenting the scene matters so much here — photos of the hazard, witness names, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage from the business can make a real difference. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened and explain your options, at no upfront cost to you.
commonInjuries: Wrist and forearm fractures from bracing a fall

Shoulder dislocations and rotator cuff tears

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Premises Liability Case

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timely Evidence
items.desc: Because California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard, early photos, incident reports, and witness contact info can be critical. An attorney can help you gather this before it disappears.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many hotels, restaurants, and retail stores in Palm Springs overwrite security video within days or weeks. A prompt preservation letter from an attorney can help stop that footage from being deleted.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for not seeing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to pursue compensation, just reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help present your side clearly.

items.question: I fell at a Palm Springs hotel or resort — is that different from a regular store?
items.answer: Hotels and resorts have the same basic duty to maintain reasonably safe conditions for guests as any other property owner. The claim process can involve additional layers, though, like resort management companies or third-party maintenance contractors. An attorney can help sort out who's actually responsible.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a government-owned property, like a city sidewalk or public building, have a much shorter window. It's worth having a conversation with an attorney sooner rather than later so evidence and deadlines aren't lost.

items.question: What if the store says they didn't know about the spill or hazard?
items.answer: That's often the central dispute in these cases, since California law requires showing the owner had notice of the condition. Things like how long the hazard was there, prior complaints, cleaning logs, or surveillance video can help establish that notice. This is exactly the kind of evidence an independent attorney can help track down.
